source: Sudarshana's summary of the classical readings (Brihat Samhita, Hora Sara, Jataka Parijata and the nakshatra tradition)

readings.about: Ashwini is the first nakshatra of the zodiac, spanning 0°–13°20′ of Aries, and so it carries the energy of every beginning. Its deities are the Ashwini Kumaras, the twin horse-headed physicians of the gods who arrive at dawn to heal and rescue. Ruled by Ketu and symbolised by a horse's head, it stands for speed, initiative, fresh starts and swift healing. It is a light and quick (kshipra) star: what is begun under it moves fast.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Ashwini the person comes across as quick, youthful and restless, often with an energetic, athletic build and a bright, open face. They act first and think on the move, love to start things and to be the first on the scene, and can have a natural gift for healing, medicine or rescue work. Patience and follow-through are the lessons.
readings.moon: The Moon in Ashwini (the janma nakshatra) gives a mind that is eager, spontaneous and hungry for new experience. Feelings rise and pass quickly; the person bounces back from setbacks, likes independence and dislikes being kept waiting. They are often helpful in a crisis and drawn to remedies, travel and speed, but can be impulsive or impatient with slow people.
readings.sun: The Sun in Ashwini (mid-late April) holds its deepest exaltation point, 10° Aries, giving confidence, courage and a strong will to lead. The soul's purpose is tied to pioneering, healing or reviving what is worn out. Such people want to be seen as capable and first; pride and haste must be watched so that their vitality serves others.

readings.about: Bharani spans 13°20′–26°40′ of Aries and is ruled by Venus, with Yama, the lord of death and dharma, as its deity. Its symbol is the yoni, the womb, and it is the star of bearing: carrying life, desire and responsibility through to birth or completion. It holds the extremes of creation and ending, pleasure and restraint. It is a fierce (ugra) star of intensity, endurance and moral weight.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Bharani the person has a strong, magnetic presence and a determined, sometimes stubborn temperament. They carry burdens others cannot and take life seriously, with strong appetites for pleasure, beauty and experience. They often face transformative events early, and grow into people of judgement who are not afraid of taboo subjects.
readings.moon: The Moon in Bharani gives deep, intense emotions and strong likes and dislikes. The person is loyal, sensual and creative, and feels a duty to see things through. They can be possessive or swing between indulgence and restraint, but they have great inner endurance and can hold space for birth, death and change.
readings.sun: The Sun in Bharani (late April-early May) is exalted in Aries, giving moral strength, resolve and a sense of personal responsibility. The life purpose often involves handling serious matters, such as justice, finance, life-and-death decisions or the arts of desire. Their authority is earned by bearing weight; harshness or judgement of others is the shadow.

readings.about: Krittika spans 26°40′ of Aries to 10° Taurus and is ruled by the Sun, with Agni, the god of fire, as its deity. Its symbol is a razor or flame, and it is the star of cutting: purifying, separating truth from falsehood, and cooking raw things into usable form. The six Krittikas (the Pleiades) nursed Kartikeya, the warrior son of Shiva, so it is both fierce and nurturing. It is a mixed (mishra) star of sharpness, purity and protection.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Krittika the person looks sharp and bright-eyed, with a dignified and often proud manner. They are direct, critical and honest to the point of bluntness, and have a strong sense of right and wrong. They make good leaders, critics, cooks, soldiers and teachers, protective of those in their care but quick to cut off what offends them.
readings.moon: The Moon in Krittika gives a mind that is determined, discerning and easily stirred. In the Aries part it is fiery and impatient; in the Taurus part (where the Moon is exalted) steadier, warmer and fond of good food and comfort. The person nurtures fiercely, holds high standards and can wound with words when hurt.
readings.sun: The Sun in Krittika (mid-May) is in its own nakshatra, giving radiance, ambition and a will to purify and lead. The soul seeks to be a source of light and truth. Such people often carry authority with ease, though stubbornness and a burning temper need tending.

readings.about: Rohini spans 10°–23°20′ of Taurus and is ruled by the Moon, with Prajapati Brahma, the creator, as its deity. Its symbol is an ox cart or chariot, and it was the Moon's favourite wife, so it is the star of growth, fertility, beauty and abundance. The Moon's moolatrikona falls in it, and it is one of the most fertile and creative nakshatras. It is a fixed (dhruva) star, good for building, planting and anything meant to last.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Rohini the person is attractive, graceful and charming, often with beautiful eyes and a pleasing voice. They love comfort, beauty, art and nature, and draw people and resources towards them. They are steady and sensual but can become attached to possessions or prone to jealousy.
readings.moon: The Moon in Rohini is very well placed: the mind is calm, creative, affectionate and enjoys the good things of life. The person is emotionally rich, artistic, domestic and fond of growing things. Their charm wins support easily; indulgence, possessiveness and a wish to be adored are the shadows.
readings.sun: The Sun in Rohini (late May-early June) gives a creative, productive soul who wants to make things flourish. They are drawn to the arts, agriculture, food, fashion or wealth-building, and seek recognition for what they create. Steady and persistent, they can also be materialistic or resistant to change.

readings.about: Mrigashira spans 23°20′ of Taurus to 6°40′ of Gemini and is ruled by Mars, with Soma, the Moon god, as its deity. Its symbol is a deer's head, and it is the star of searching: the curious, gentle, ever-moving quest for what delights the mind. It joins earthy Taurus and airy Gemini, sensual pleasure and intellectual enquiry. It is a soft (mridu) star, good for friendship, travel, learning and the arts.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Mrigashira the person is slender, alert and youthful-looking, with an inquisitive, wandering mind. They love to research, travel, talk and explore, and are gentle and sociable but restless. They can be indecisive or suspicious, always looking for something better around the next corner.
readings.moon: The Moon in Mrigashira gives a curious, sensitive and playful mind that is easily bored. The person seeks variety in ideas, places and company, is charming and witty, and has a love of music, travel and study. Their restlessness can turn to anxiety or doubt unless they find a worthwhile quest.
readings.sun: The Sun in Mrigashira (early-mid June) gives a soul driven to seek knowledge and experience. They are often writers, researchers, travellers or communicators, and want recognition for their cleverness. Their task is to commit to a path instead of always searching.

readings.about: Ardra spans 6°40′–20° of Gemini and is ruled by Rahu, with Rudra, the fierce storm form of Shiva, as its deity. Its symbol is a teardrop or a diamond, and it is the star of the storm: destruction that clears the air, grief that leads to renewal, effort that brings insight. Its star is Betelgeuse, the red giant in Orion. It is a sharp (tikshna) star of intensity, research and transformation through hardship.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Ardra the person has a sharp, probing intellect and an intense, sometimes stormy nature. They question everything, are drawn to science, technology, research or psychology, and are not afraid of chaos. Life brings upheavals that make them stronger; they can be blunt, moody or rebellious.
readings.moon: The Moon in Ardra gives a mind of strong emotions, deep thought and a need to understand. The person can feel intensely, experience periods of turmoil or grief, and come through them wiser and more compassionate. They are often brilliant, unconventional and truthful, though restless and quick to anger.
readings.sun: The Sun in Ardra (late June) gives a soul that seeks truth through effort and upheaval. They are drawn to fields that break things down to rebuild them better: research, analysis, technology, healing of deep wounds. Recognition comes after struggle; arrogance and destructiveness are the dangers.

readings.about: Punarvasu spans 20° of Gemini to 3°20′ of Cancer and is ruled by Jupiter, with Aditi, the boundless mother of the gods, as its deity. Its symbol is a quiver of arrows or a house, and its name means 'return of the light': renewal, coming home, and goodness restored after trouble. Lord Rama was born in it, and it carries gentleness, faith and generosity. It is a movable (chara) star, good for travel, beginnings again and restoration.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Punarvasu the person is kind, optimistic and generous, with a gentle, forgiving nature. They are content with simple things, recover easily from losses and often return to their roots. They make good teachers, counsellors and hosts, though they can be too trusting or lack ambition.
readings.moon: The Moon in Punarvasu gives a mind that is hopeful, philosophical and nurturing. The person has a strong attachment to home and family, a love of learning and travel, and a capacity to start over again and again. They are easily satisfied and kind, but may be fickle or slow to act.
readings.sun: The Sun in Punarvasu (early-mid July) gives a soul whose purpose is to restore and to teach. They seek a life of meaning, often in education, religion, counselling or travel, and want to be recognised as good. Wisdom and integrity are their light; naivety is the shadow.

readings.about: Pushya spans 3°20′–16°40′ of Cancer and is ruled by Saturn, with Brihaspati, the guru of the gods, as its deity. Its symbol is a cow's udder or a lotus, and it is the star of nourishment: support, care, devotion and spiritual growth. It is considered one of the most auspicious nakshatras, and Jupiter is exalted in the sign it occupies. It is a light (laghu) star, very good for beginnings, rituals and anything nurturing.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Pushya the person is caring, responsible and dependable, with a calm, protective manner. They respect tradition, family and religion, and like to support and guide others. They make good teachers, advisers, managers and caregivers, though they can be conservative or worry too much.
readings.moon: The Moon in Pushya gives a mind that is nurturing, devoted and emotionally stable. The person is helpful, disciplined and content, with a strong attachment to home and duty. They find fulfilment in serving others; over-protectiveness and self-sacrifice are the risks.
readings.sun: The Sun in Pushya (late July) gives a soul whose purpose is to nourish and uphold. They are drawn to service, teaching, religion, government or care work, and value respectability. Their authority is built on reliability; rigidity or self-righteousness is the shadow.

readings.about: Ashlesha spans 16°40′–30° of Cancer and is ruled by Mercury, with the Nagas, the serpent deities, as its deity. Its symbol is a coiled serpent, and it is the star of embrace: binding, entwining, hypnotic power and kundalini energy. It is the last nakshatra of a water sign (a gandanta point), so it carries deep, hidden and intense forces. It is a sharp (tikshna) star of strategy, secrecy and penetrating insight.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Ashlesha the person has piercing eyes and a magnetic, mysterious presence. They are shrewd, perceptive and strategic, good at reading people and handling secrets. They can be secretive, manipulative or suspicious, but also deeply loyal to those they let in, and gifted in psychology, medicine or occult study.
readings.moon: The Moon in Ashlesha gives a mind that is intense, intuitive and self-protective. The person feels deeply but guards it, can be clingy or controlling in relationships, and has strong instincts about others' motives. With maturity this becomes wisdom and healing power; unchecked it becomes suspicion and manipulation.
readings.sun: The Sun in Ashlesha (early-mid August) gives a soul that seeks power through knowledge and influence. They are drawn to politics, strategy, research, medicine or the occult. Their intelligence is formidable; they must use it to protect rather than to bind others.

readings.about: Magha spans 0°–13°20′ of Leo and is ruled by Ketu, with the Pitris, the ancestral fathers, as its deity. Its symbol is a royal throne, and it is the star of lineage: royalty, heritage, honour and the power passed down from the ancestors. Its brightest star is Regulus, the heart of the Lion. It is a fierce (ugra) star of authority, tradition and pride.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Magha the person has a regal bearing and a strong sense of dignity and status. They respect tradition and their family line, seek positions of authority, and like to be treated with respect. They can be generous and noble, but also proud, arrogant or quick to take offence.
readings.moon: The Moon in Magha gives a mind that wants honour, recognition and a sense of belonging to something great. The person is devoted to family and ancestry, enjoys ceremony and luxury, and is often generous to those who serve them. Pride and a need for approval are the weak points.
readings.sun: The Sun in Magha (mid-late August) is in its own sign, Leo, giving leadership, dignity and ambition. The soul's purpose is to carry a legacy and to lead with honour. Such people rise to high positions, but must avoid vanity and living only on past glory.

readings.about: Purva Phalguni spans 13°20′–26°40′ of Leo and is ruled by Venus, with Bhaga, the god of fortune, pleasure and marital bliss, as its deity. Its symbol is the front legs of a bed or a hammock, and it is the star of rest and enjoyment: love, romance, creativity and the pleasures earned after work. It is a fierce (ugra) star by classification but sweet in nature, ruling relationships and the arts.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Purva Phalguni the person is charming, warm, sociable and fond of beauty and comfort. They are generous, playful and creative, love parties and romance, and attract people easily. They can be lazy, vain or indulgent, but bring joy wherever they go.
readings.moon: The Moon in Purva Phalguni gives a mind that seeks pleasure, love and creative expression. The person is affectionate, artistic and good-humoured, and values relationships highly. They need rest and fun to feel balanced; over-indulgence and a dislike of hard work are the risks.
readings.sun: The Sun in Purva Phalguni (early September) gives a soul that wants to shine through creativity, love and generosity. They are drawn to the arts, entertainment, hospitality or luxury. Their warmth wins hearts; self-indulgence and pride are the shadows.

readings.about: Uttara Phalguni spans 26°40′ of Leo to 10° of Virgo and is ruled by the Sun, with Aryaman, the god of contracts, friendship and patronage, as its deity. Its symbol is the back legs of a bed, and it is the star of partnership and patronage: commitment, union, kindness and lasting help. It completes the pair begun by Purva Phalguni, turning pleasure into commitment. It is a fixed (dhruva) star, good for marriage, agreements and lasting work.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Uttara Phalguni the person is reliable, generous, honest and helpful, with a dignified, friendly manner. They make loyal friends and partners, and often work in service, administration or counselling. They seek stability and respect; overwork or dependence on others' approval can be issues.
readings.moon: The Moon in Uttara Phalguni gives a mind that is kind, responsible and committed. The person values friendship and marriage, likes to help, and is good at organising and keeping promises. They feel secure in stable partnerships; rigidity and over-giving are the risks.
readings.sun: The Sun in Uttara Phalguni (mid-September) is in its own nakshatra, giving a soul devoted to service, leadership through kindness and lasting achievements. They often rise through patronage and good alliances, and are drawn to government, management or social work.

readings.about: Hasta spans 10°–23°20′ of Virgo and is ruled by the Moon, with Savitar, the creative, inspiring aspect of the Sun, as its deity. Its symbol is an open hand, and it is the star of skill: craftsmanship, dexterity, healing hands and the ability to grasp and manifest what one seeks. It is a light and quick (kshipra) star, good for trade, crafts, medicine and learning.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Hasta the person is clever, practical and skilful with their hands, with a witty and charming manner. They are industrious, resourceful and good at business, crafts, healing or writing. They can be restless, critical or overly calculating, but they get things done.
readings.moon: The Moon in Hasta gives a mind that is quick, clever and practical, with a gift for humour and fine work. The person is hard-working, helpful and adaptable, and often good at healing or handicrafts. Nervousness, worry and a need for control are the weak points.
readings.sun: The Sun in Hasta (late September-early October) gives a soul that seeks mastery through skill and service. They are drawn to crafts, medicine, commerce, technology or teaching. Their success comes through hard work and precision; perfectionism can hold them back.

readings.about: Chitra spans 23°20′ of Virgo to 6°40′ of Libra and is ruled by Mars, with Tvashtar (Vishvakarma), the celestial architect, as its deity. Its symbol is a bright jewel or pearl, and its star is Spica, one of the brightest in the sky. It is the star of design: beauty, form, architecture and the art of making things brilliant. It is a soft (mridu) star, good for the arts, fashion and building.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Chitra the person is attractive, stylish and eye-catching, with beautiful eyes and a strong sense of design. They are creative, charismatic and ambitious, often working in design, architecture, engineering, fashion or the arts. They can be vain, self-centred or overly concerned with appearances.
readings.moon: The Moon in Chitra gives a mind that loves beauty, creativity and self-expression. The person is energetic, artistic and charming, wants to be admired, and is good at making things look good. Restlessness, vanity and a love of display are the risks.
readings.sun: The Sun in Chitra (mid-October) is debilitated in Libra for its later half, but the soul still seeks brilliance through creation. They are drawn to design, engineering, art and anything that lasts as a work. Ego is softened by partnership; they shine when they work with others.

readings.about: Swati spans 6°40′–20° of Libra and is ruled by Rahu, with Vayu, the wind god, as its deity. Its symbol is a young sprout swaying in the wind or a coral, and it is the star of independence: flexibility, movement, trade and the ability to scatter and spread. Its star is Arcturus. It is a movable (chara) star, good for travel, trade, learning and new ventures.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Swati the person is graceful, courteous, diplomatic and independent. They value freedom, adapt easily and are often good at business and negotiation. They can be indecisive or restless, but they bend without breaking and do well on their own terms.
readings.moon: The Moon in Swati gives a mind that is balanced, sociable and freedom-loving. The person is kind, fair and adaptable, enjoys learning and travel, and needs space to grow. Their emotions can blow hot and cold; dependence on circumstances and indecision are the risks.
readings.sun: The Sun in Swati (late October-early November) is debilitated in Libra, most deeply here, so the soul's light must work through cooperation, diplomacy and flexibility. They are drawn to trade, law, travel or the arts. Independence of mind brings them success.

readings.about: Vishakha spans 20° of Libra to 3°20′ of Scorpio and is ruled by Jupiter, with Indra and Agni, the twin gods of power and fire, as its deities. Its symbol is a triumphal arch or a potter's wheel, and it is the star of purpose: single-minded ambition, achievement and reaching the goal. It is a mixed (mishra) star of determination, competition and eventual triumph.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Vishakha the person is ambitious, determined and goal-oriented, with strong energy and drive. They are often eloquent and attractive, and fight hard for what they want. They can be competitive, jealous or impatient, but they reach their goals in the end.
readings.moon: The Moon in Vishakha gives a mind that is focused, ambitious and passionate. The person seeks success, is driven to achieve, and can be single-minded to the point of obsession. In the Scorpio part the Moon is debilitated, making feelings more intense; patience and contentment are the lessons.
readings.sun: The Sun in Vishakha (mid-November) gives a soul with a mission. They seek achievement and are drawn to leadership, politics, research or religion. Their determination is a great strength; frustration and the means used to reach the goal need watching.

readings.about: Anuradha spans 3°20′–16°40′ of Scorpio and is ruled by Saturn, with Mitra, the god of friendship and cooperation, as its deity. Its symbol is a lotus or a triumphal archway, and it is the star of devotion: friendship, cooperation, loyalty and success through working with others. It is a soft (mridu) star, good for friendship, groups, travel and spiritual practice.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Anuradha the person is friendly, loyal, disciplined and devoted, with a talent for organisation and working with groups. They often travel or live away from home, and succeed through friendship and perseverance. They can be moody or jealous, but their dedication is deep.
readings.moon: The Moon in Anuradha gives a mind that is devoted, sensitive and emotionally deep, though the Moon is debilitated in Scorpio. The person values friendship and loyalty, has spiritual leanings, and finds success through cooperation. Melancholy and possessiveness are the shadows.
readings.sun: The Sun in Anuradha (late November) gives a soul whose purpose is cooperation, friendship and devotion. They are drawn to organisations, diplomacy, research, occult study or spiritual paths. Success comes through persistence and alliances.

readings.about: Jyeshtha spans 16°40′–30° of Scorpio and is ruled by Mercury, with Indra, the king of the gods, as its deity. Its symbol is a circular amulet or an umbrella, and its name means 'the eldest': seniority, protection, power and the responsibility that comes with it. Its star is Antares, the heart of the Scorpion. It is a sharp (tikshna) star and a gandanta point, intense and protective.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Jyeshtha the person carries seniority and responsibility early, with a protective, commanding presence. They are clever, resourceful and capable, often the one others rely on. They can be secretive, proud or irritable, and may feel isolated by their position.
readings.moon: The Moon in Jyeshtha gives a mind that is intense, protective and sharp. The person feels responsible for others, has strong pride and a sense of honour, and can be self-reliant to the point of loneliness. Jealousy and a need to control are the risks; generosity is the cure.
readings.sun: The Sun in Jyeshtha (early December) gives a soul that seeks authority and the role of protector. They are drawn to leadership, management, the military or occult study. Their courage is great; they must use power with humility.

readings.about: Mula spans 0°–13°20′ of Sagittarius and is ruled by Ketu, with Nirriti, the goddess of dissolution, as its deity. Its symbol is a bunch of roots tied together, and it is the star of the root: getting to the bottom of things, uprooting, and finding the foundation of truth. It lies towards the centre of the galaxy and is a gandanta point. It is a sharp (tikshna) star of research, destruction of the false and spiritual seeking.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Mula the person is probing, philosophical and independent, with a strong urge to find the truth. They are often researchers, investigators, healers or spiritual seekers. Life can bring sudden losses that uproot them; they can be blunt or rebellious but are deeply sincere.
readings.moon: The Moon in Mula gives a mind that questions everything and seeks the root cause. The person is intense, honest and adventurous, and may go through upheavals in family or home life. They are attracted to philosophy, herbs, medicine and the occult; restlessness and destructiveness are the shadows.
readings.sun: The Sun in Mula (mid-late December) gives a soul whose purpose is to seek fundamental truths. They are drawn to research, philosophy, religion, medicine or investigation. Their courage to tear down the false is their gift; nihilism is the danger.

readings.about: Purva Ashadha spans 13°20′–26°40′ of Sagittarius and is ruled by Venus, with Apas, the goddess of the waters, as its deity. Its symbol is a fan or a winnowing basket, and it is the star of invincibility: early victory, purification, conviction and the power to declare. It is a fierce (ugra) star of pride, persuasion and energy, good for confronting enemies and for water rites.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Purva Ashadha the person is confident, persuasive and proud, with strong convictions and a charming manner. They love to win debates, champion causes and inspire others. They can be stubborn or overconfident, but their enthusiasm carries people with them.
readings.moon: The Moon in Purva Ashadha gives a mind that is idealistic, optimistic and emotionally strong. The person is loyal, fond of travel and water, and holds to their beliefs. They can be proud or argumentative; humility makes their victories last.
readings.sun: The Sun in Purva Ashadha (late December-early January) gives a soul that seeks victory and recognition through its convictions. They are drawn to law, philosophy, teaching, the arts or anything to do with water. Their persuasiveness is a great asset; arrogance is the risk.

readings.about: Uttara Ashadha spans 26°40′ of Sagittarius to 10° of Capricorn and is ruled by the Sun, with the Vishvadevas, the universal gods of virtue, as its deities. Its symbol is an elephant's tusk or a small bed, and it is the star of final victory: lasting achievement won through righteousness and steady effort. Abhijit, the hidden 28th nakshatra, falls in its last part. It is a fixed (dhruva) star, good for lasting works and commitments.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Uttara Ashadha the person is principled, responsible and persevering, with a dignified, honest manner. They take on great tasks and complete them, earn respect slowly, and are loyal and ethical. They can be rigid or serious, but they win in the end.
readings.moon: The Moon in Uttara Ashadha gives a mind that is steady, ethical and committed. The person is grateful, dutiful and reliable, and holds high ideals. They may feel lonely at the top; rigidity and stubbornness are the risks.
readings.sun: The Sun in Uttara Ashadha (mid-late January) is in its own nakshatra, giving a soul devoted to dharma and lasting achievement. They are drawn to leadership, government, law or social causes, and their success comes late but surely.

readings.about: Shravana spans 10°–23°20′ of Capricorn and is ruled by the Moon, with Vishnu, the preserver, as its deity. Its symbol is an ear or three footprints, and it is the star of listening: learning through hearing, connection, wisdom and the preservation of knowledge. It is a movable (chara) star, good for learning, travel, communication and spiritual practice.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Shravana the person is a good listener, thoughtful, learned and well-spoken, with a modest, polite manner. They value knowledge and tradition, and often work in teaching, counselling, media or travel. They can be sensitive to criticism or gossip, but they earn respect through wisdom.
readings.moon: The Moon in Shravana gives a mind that absorbs knowledge, listens deeply and seeks connection. The person is wise, devoted, and often religious or philosophical, with a love of music and learning. Sensitivity to others' words and a tendency to worry are the shadows.
readings.sun: The Sun in Shravana (late January-early February) gives a soul whose purpose is to learn, preserve and pass on knowledge. They are drawn to education, media, religion or counselling. Success comes through listening well and building a good name.

readings.about: Dhanishtha spans 23°20′ of Capricorn to 6°40′ of Aquarius and is ruled by Mars, with the eight Vasus, the gods of abundance and the elements, as its deities. Its symbol is a drum, and it is the star of rhythm and wealth: music, abundance, fame and the ability to work together in harmony. It is a movable (chara) star, good for music, wealth, travel and group work.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Dhanishtha the person is energetic, ambitious and talented, often musical or athletic, with a lively, generous presence. They are good with groups, finance and organisation. They can be proud, materialistic or impatient, but they shine in public.
readings.moon: The Moon in Dhanishtha gives a mind that is confident, generous and rhythmic, with a love of music and dance. The person is sociable and good at teamwork, and often achieves wealth and recognition. They can be restless or vain; their marriage life may need extra care.
readings.sun: The Sun in Dhanishtha (mid-February) gives a soul that seeks fame and abundance through talent and teamwork. They are drawn to music, sports, real estate, finance or the military. Their ambition is strong; arrogance is the shadow.

readings.about: Shatabhisha spans 6°40′–20° of Aquarius and is ruled by Rahu, with Varuna, the god of the cosmic waters and divine law, as its deity. Its symbol is an empty circle, and its name means 'a hundred healers' or 'a hundred stars': healing, secrecy, science and the search for the hidden. It is a movable (chara) star, good for healing, research, technology and solitary work.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Shatabhisha the person is independent, secretive, philosophical and often scientific, with a reserved presence. They are drawn to healing, research, technology or astrology, and can work alone for long periods. They may seem aloof or stubborn, but they are truthful and visionary.
readings.moon: The Moon in Shatabhisha gives a mind that is reflective, private and truth-seeking. The person may feel lonely or misunderstood, but has deep insight and healing ability. They are honest and principled; moodiness and withdrawal are the risks.
readings.sun: The Sun in Shatabhisha (late February-early March) gives a soul whose purpose is to heal and to uncover hidden truths. They are drawn to medicine, science, technology, astrology or reform. Their vision is ahead of its time; isolation is the shadow.

readings.about: Purva Bhadrapada spans 20° of Aquarius to 3°20′ of Pisces and is ruled by Jupiter, with Aja Ekapada, the one-footed goat, a fiery form of Rudra, as its deity. Its symbol is the front legs of a funeral cot or a two-faced man, and it is the star of fire and transformation: intense spiritual zeal, idealism and burning away the old. It is a fierce (ugra) star of passion, sacrifice and radical change.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Purva Bhadrapada the person is intense, idealistic and passionate, with a serious and sometimes two-sided nature. They are drawn to causes, spirituality, occult study or reform, and can be generous and visionary. They can also be anxious, extreme or cynical when their ideals are let down.
readings.moon: The Moon in Purva Bhadrapada gives a mind of strong emotions, high ideals and a sense of mission. The person can swing between worldly and spiritual pulls, and may be nervous or worry about the future. With focus, they become powerful agents of change.
readings.sun: The Sun in Purva Bhadrapada (early-mid March) gives a soul that seeks transformation and higher truth. They are drawn to spirituality, philanthropy, reform, research or the occult. Their zeal inspires others; fanaticism is the danger.

readings.about: Uttara Bhadrapada spans 3°20′–16°40′ of Pisces and is ruled by Saturn, with Ahir Budhnya, the serpent of the deep waters, as its deity. Its symbol is the back legs of a funeral cot or a twin, and it is the star of depth: calm wisdom, patience, renunciation and the stillness beneath the waves. It is a fixed (dhruva) star, good for lasting works, meditation and spiritual practice.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Uttara Bhadrapada the person is calm, wise, disciplined and kind, with a deep and steady presence. They control their emotions well, are generous and charitable, and are drawn to spirituality, counselling or research. They can be reclusive or slow to act, but they are reliable.
readings.moon: The Moon in Uttara Bhadrapada gives a mind that is deep, peaceful and self-controlled. The person is compassionate, patient and wise beyond their years, with a love of solitude and meditation. They may hide their feelings; depression or inertia are the shadows.
readings.sun: The Sun in Uttara Bhadrapada (late March-early April) gives a soul whose purpose is wisdom, service and spiritual depth. They are drawn to religion, counselling, research or charity. Their strength is patience; their light grows over time.

readings.about: Revati spans 16°40′–30° of Pisces and is ruled by Mercury, with Pushan, the nourisher and protector of travellers and flocks, as its deity. Its symbol is a fish or a drum, and it is the star of safe passage: nourishment, protection, journeys and the completion of the zodiac's cycle. It is the last nakshatra and a gandanta point, where the journey ends and the next begins. It is a soft (mridu) star, good for travel, friendship and the arts.
readings.lagna: With the Lagna in Revati the person is gentle, kind, imaginative and well-liked, with a soft, sympathetic presence. They care for others, love travel and the arts, and often have spiritual leanings. They can be over-sensitive, impractical or easily hurt, but they bring comfort to many.
readings.moon: The Moon in Revati gives a mind that is compassionate, intuitive and imaginative. The person is nurturing and generous, loves animals and travel, and is drawn to the spiritual. Their sensitivity is a gift; escapism and being taken advantage of are the risks.
readings.sun: The Sun in Revati (early April, just before it enters Aries) gives a soul whose purpose is to nourish, guide and complete. They are drawn to the arts, travel, care work, religion or anything that helps others cross over safely. Their kindness is their power.
